jurisdictions.name: Nevada
jurisdictions.note: Present in the RCFP list and absent from several other 2026 compilations. Nevada case law distinguishes telephone from in-person. Treat as all-party.

jurisdictions.name: Connecticut
jurisdictions.note: All-party for telephone recordings but one-party in person under criminal law. Treat as all-party.

jurisdictions.name: Oregon
jurisdictions.note: All-party for in-person oral communications, one-party for electronic. The distinction does not map cleanly onto a video call.

jurisdictions.name: Michigan
jurisdictions.note: The statute reads all-party but Michigan courts have held a participant may record. Unsettled.

jurisdictions.name: Hawaii
jurisdictions.note: One-party generally, all-party for recordings in a private place. Treat as all-party.

jurisdictions.name: Germany
jurisdictions.note: Criminal. Applies to participants as well as third parties; fines or up to three years' imprisonment.

jurisdictions.name: France
jurisdictions.note: Criminal. Up to one year and a EUR 45,000 fine.

jurisdictions.name: United Kingdom
jurisdictions.note: Recording is processing of personal data and needs a lawful basis. Employee consent is generally invalid due to power imbalance.

jurisdictions.name: Ireland
jurisdictions.note: As UK: a lawful basis is required and employee consent is generally invalid.

jurisdictions.name: Netherlands
jurisdictions.note: A participant may record, but processing still needs a lawful basis.

jurisdictions.name: Spain
jurisdictions.note: A lawful basis is required.

jurisdictions.name: Italy
jurisdictions.note: A lawful basis is required.

jurisdictions.name: Canada
jurisdictions.note: One-party consent for interception, but PIPEDA separately requires knowledge and consent. Quebec, BC and Alberta add provincial rules.

jurisdictions.name: Australia
jurisdictions.statute: Surveillance Devices Acts (per state and territory)
jurisdictions.note: A per-state patchwork: some jurisdictions require all-party consent and others permit one-party. Treat as all-party.

jurisdictions.name: New Zealand
jurisdictions.note: A participant may record.

jurisdictions.name: Japan
jurisdictions.statute: Act on the Protection of Personal Information
jurisdictions.note: A participant may record; APPI still governs the resulting data.

jurisdictions.name: Singapore
jurisdictions.note: Consent is required to collect personal data, with exceptions.

jurisdictions.name: India
jurisdictions.note: Consent-based framework for personal data.

jurisdictions.name: Brazil
jurisdictions.statute: Lei Geral de Protecao de Dados (LGPD)
jurisdictions.note: A lawful basis is required.
